headline: FIRE CREW — the lost cry through the smoke
lede: The arcade's split-information law had one direction: light finds people. Now sound answers back — hidden victims wail omnidirectionally across their own floor, five tiles at a time, so a seat can hear what it cannot see. The never-dry kick aimed at FIRE CREW again this shift (its #1712 DISCLAIMER marker was malformed and kept scoring a decided state as weakness), so the marker got its doctrine shape and one real gameplay fix shipped with it.

notes.text: cryAt/helpCry in sim.js: a still-hidden victim cries across its own floor up to 5 tiles — found, carried, saved and lost are silence, and no voice crosses the loft decking. Per-seat like lightAt: on a shared device only the seat standing in earshot hears.

step() names a new voice once per victim for human seats — SOMEONE'S IN THERE - LISTEN — while cpu seats and a seated WATCH stay silent (the #2989 hands-off law). The repeated locating cry rides the sim's own cadence at half-second pairs, pitch and weight climbing as the voice nears.

firecrewcheck 228/0 (+27 gates incl. the audible-but-unlit band as real geometry and six src pins), firecrewplay DRIVE GREEN with 7 new real-tick legs, datasetcheck byte-exact 84/84, five mutants die by name. The cry never touches stateHash — replays verify untouched.

QA edges: per-seat earshot should read on a 2P keyboard shift (seat 2 hears its own band, seat 1 does not); ping-pong crossings re-cry by design but spam the card once; a drawn marker stays illegal — a pin would leak the position the light law denies.
